note: The why names the sound to listen for (IV steps away, V leans home), so the learner can use it on any song. Each block turns the same listening drill a new way: two chords, all three, then a new key.

exercise.title: Hear the 4 and the 5 coming
exercise.focus: I IV V by ear · G major, then D major · guess before you look
exercise.why: The IV chord sounds like stepping away from home and the V like leaning back towards it, so that pull tells you which chord is playing in any song.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the chords: G and C take turns, then G and D. Listen to how C steps away from G and how D leans back towards it, and call out which one you hear.
Now all three chords, in a new order. Look away from the chord boxes and call out 1, 4 or 5 on each change, then look to check. Keep going until you hear it before you think it.
The same order in D major: the chords are new, but the pull is the same, so keep calling out the numbers. Then put on a song you know and listen for the 4 and the 5.
